en: Back when I first became a retreat speaker
and started leading retreats.

text:
처음에 수련회가
몇 개 없을 때는 괜찮았는데
en: With only a few retreats, I was fine.

text:
수련회가 많을 때는
일주일, 일주일, 이주일이
en: But with many, a week, another week, two weeks —
a whole summer could be retreats.

text:
그러면 *말씀*을 전하죠
사람들이 막 은혜를 받습니다
en: I'd preach, and people were deeply moved.
I'd lead prayer meetings and we'd pray together,
and you feel so full.

text:
근데 일주일, 이주일 그렇게
*연속*으로 수련회를 하면
en: But after one, two weeks of retreats in a row,
something starts to sink.
At first I didn't get it. I really didn't.
I thought I was just physically tired.
Later I realized.

text:
수련회를 막 하니까
*개인 기도* 시간이 없거든요
en: Running retreats left no time for my own prayer.

text:
설교를 막 하니까
그리고 막 은혜를 받으니까
en: Preaching, people being moved,
I thought praying up there counted as praying.
That's how you fall.
Countless pastors have fallen that way.
Even yesterday, preparing my sermon,
I stopped to pray through a psalm.
Preparing a sermon is one thing;

text:
그것이 내 *영혼*의 무언가를
채워주는 것은 *다른 문제*죠
en: filling my own soul is another.
I realized a retreat
isn't where I get filled.

text:
막 *붕붕* 떠 있다가
망하는 사람 많습니다
en: Many people ride a high, then crash.
Always be on guard.
